items.stem: Find the first four terms of the sequence given by the recursive rule $u_{1} = 1$, $u_{n} = 2u_{n-1} + 3$ for $n \geq 2$.
Find the explicit formula for the n-th term of the GP: 5, 25, 125, ...
items.answer: First term $a = 5$, common ratio $r = 5$. Explicit formula: $t_{n} = 5 \times 5^{(n-1)} = 5^{n}$.

items.stem: Consider the sequence given by the explicit rule $t_{n} = 3n - 7$. (i) Find its 12th term. (ii) Which term of the sequence is 332?
An AP consists of 50 terms in which the 3rd term is 12 and the last term is 106. Find the 29th term.
Determine whether 0 is a term of the AP: 21, 18, 15, ...
items.answer: $a = 21$, $d = -3$. Set $a_{n} = 0$: $21 + (n-1)(-3) = 0 \Rightarrow 21 = 3(n-1) \Rightarrow n - 1 = 7 \Rightarrow n = 8$. Yes, 0 is the 8th term of the AP.

items.stem: Find the sum of the first n natural numbers, $S_{n} = 1 + 2 + 3 + \ldots + n$.
items.answer: Let $S_{n} = 1 + 2 + \ldots + n$ and reverse the order: $S_{n} = n + (n-1) + \ldots + 1$. Adding term by term, $2S_{n} = (n+1)$ taken n times, so $2S_{n} = n(n+1)$ and $S_{n} = n(n+1)/2$.

items.stem: Find the 31st term of an AP whose 11th term is 38 and 16th term is 73.
The sum of the first three terms of a GP is 26, and the sum of their squares is 364. Find the terms of the GP.
items.answer: Let the terms be $a$, $ar$, $ar^{2}$, so $a(1 + r + r^{2}) = 26$ and $a^{2}(1 + r^{2} + r^{4}) = 364$. Dividing the square of the first by the second gives $(1 + r + r^{2})/(1 - r + r^{2}) = 13/7$, leading to $3r^{2} - 10r + 3 = 0$, so $r = 3$ or $r = 1/3$. If $r = 3$: $13a = 26 \Rightarrow a = 2$, terms 2, 6, 18. If $r = 1/3$: terms 18, 6, 2.

items.stem: If the first term and the $n^{\mathrm{th}}$ term of a G.P. are a and b respectively, and P is the product of the first n terms, then prove that $P^{2} = (ab)^{n}$.
items.answer: $P = a \times (ar) \times (ar^{2}) \times \ldots \times (ar^{n-1}) = a^{n} \times r^{(0+1+\ldots+n-1)}$, and the sum of exponents of r is $n(n-1)/2$. So $P = a^{n} r^{n(n-1)/2}$ and $P^{2} = a^{2n} r^{n(n-1)} = [a^{2}r^{n-1}]^{n} = [a \times (ar^{n-1})]^{n} = (ab)^{n}$.

items.stem: The 4th, 6th and last term of a G.P. are 10, 40 and 640 respectively. If the common ratio is positive, find the first term, common ratio and the number of terms of the series.
items.answer: $ar^{3} = 10$ and $ar^{5} = 40$. Dividing, $r^{2} = 4 \Rightarrow r = 2$ (since $r > 0$). From the first, $8a = 10 \Rightarrow a = 5/4 = 1.25$. Last term: $(5/4) \times 2^{n-1} = 640 \Rightarrow 2^{n-1} = 512 = 2^{9} \Rightarrow n = 10$. First term $= 5/4$, common ratio $= 2$, number of terms $= 10$.

items.stem: How many multiples of 4 lie between 10 and 250?
items.answer: Multiples of 4 are 12, 16, 20, ..., 248, with $a = 12$, $d = 4$ and $a_{n} = 248$. Then $248 = 12 + (n-1)4 \Rightarrow 236 = 4(n-1) \Rightarrow n = 60$. There are 60 multiples of 4.

items.stem: The number of bacteria in a certain culture doubles every hour. If there were 30 bacteria present in the culture originally, how many bacteria will be present at the end of the 2nd hour, 4th hour and $n^{\mathrm{th}}$ hour?
items.answer: Initial count $a = 30$, common ratio $r = 2$, so the number at the end of hour t is $ar^{t}$. (i) End of 2nd hour $= 30 \times 2^{2} = 120$. (ii) End of 4th hour $= 30 \times 2^{4} = 480$. (iii) End of nth hour $= 30 \times 2^{n}$.

items.stem: A person books a taxi charging a fixed booking fee of ₹200 plus ₹40 per kilometre travelled. (i) Write the sequence of total fares after travelling 1 km, 2 km, 3 km, etc. (ii) Derive the explicit formula for the n-th term. (iii) Calculate the total fare for 10 km.
Which term of the A.P. $-7, -12, -17, -22, \ldots$ will be $-82$? Is $-100$ any term of the A.P.? Give reason for your answer.
items.answer: $a = -7$, $d = -5$. (i) $-7 + (n-1)(-5) = -82 \Rightarrow -5(n-1) = -75 \Rightarrow n = 16$, so $-82$ is the 16th term. (ii) $-7 + (n-1)(-5) = -100 \Rightarrow -5(n-1) = -93 \Rightarrow n = 19.6$. Since n is not a positive integer, $-100$ is not a term of the A.P.

items.stem: A ball is dropped from a height of 80 metres. After hitting the ground, it bounces back to 60% of the height from which it fell. It continues bouncing in this way. (i) Write the explicit formula for the height after the n-th bounce. (ii) What height does it reach after the 5th bounce?
items.answer: (i) The heights form a GP with first term 80 and ratio 0.6, so the height after the n-th bounce is $h_{n} = 80 \times (0.6)^{n}$. (ii) $h_{5} = 80 \times (0.6)^{5} = 80 \times 0.07776 = 6.2208$ metres.
